name: Serial number, IMEI and device ID
plain: Sites cannot read your serial number, IMEI or advertising ID.
meaning: No unprompted API exposes hardware identifiers. Managed ChromeOS and enterprise policies expose serial to allowlisted extensions only (chrome.enterprise.deviceAttributes). A regular site gets none; fingerprints are rebuilt from many signals instead.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: proxy: fingerprint hash
fields.range: combine UA, screen, fonts, GPU for an approximate ID

fields.name: proxy: Web Bluetooth or WebUSB serialNumber
fields.range: only for a device the user picked in a prompt

limits.headline: Can't see your serial number, IMEI, or advertising ID from a web page
limits.user_action: Nothing. Pages have no way to ask for this
can: Build a tracking guess from many small signals
Set its own cookie or ID that stays on your browser
Let managed work devices pass a serial to approved extensions
cannot: See your IMEI or phone ID
Get an ID that survives clearing site data on its own

story.what_it_is: Sites cannot read your serial number, IMEI or advertising ID.
story.for_you: A web page cannot see your device's serial number or phone ID. That is a big reason the web is safer to browse than many apps. Only company managed devices can reveal some of it to approved tools.
story.for_makers: Hardware IDs are the strongest way to follow a person for ads and fraud checks. The web gives no such ID, so sites use cookies, logins and fingerprints. Managed work devices can expose a serial to approved tools only.

use_cases.example: An ad network wanted the advertising ID and instead uses cookies or fingerprinting.
A fraud team wanted the serial to spot repeat abuse and builds a device profile instead.
An IT portal wanted laptop serials and needs a managed extension.
A bank wanted a permanent device ID and uses a stored device token after a login.
A game site wanted to ban cheaters by device and bans accounts and IP ranges instead.
An analytics team wanted a stable ID and settles for first party IDs.
A retailer wanted to match a phone to a past visit and relies on login.

risks: Managed devices can expose a serial

legit_uses: None: the browser deliberately withholds it
abuse: Sites attempt proxies to recover it
